title: Pose & Primer Workbench — few-shot recipe sketches
content:
Note to self:

This is a personal workbench for 'poses' (short instruction shapes) + primers (tiny scaffolding text) that we can reuse across product integrations. Intention: find compact, robust minimal-priming patterns that survive prompt drift and token-budget constraints. Keeping this intentionally messy — riff log, quick failures, and candidate templates.

Top-level goals:
- Build 3 stable pose archetypes for instruction-following (clarity, brevity, guardrails).
- Curate 4 micro few-shot sets (3 examples each) that bias for factuality / format / conservative hallucination.
- Capture recurring failure fingerprints with short repro text to feed back to evals.

Hypotheses (fast):
1) Explicit output schema in the primer reduces hallucination in off-domain queries more than increasing context tokens.
2) Two-shot with contrastive negative example helps reduce overconfident false assertions.
3) 'Role-as-constraint' (set task role + disallow verbs) reduces instruction creep in multi-step tasks.

POSES (brief instruction shapes) — short names and rationale:
- ACTION-ONLY: "Do X." Minimal. Use for high-precision transformations.
  Example: "Convert the following bullet list into a one-line summary:"

- SAID-AND-DONE: "You are a concise editor. Say what changes you made. Return only the final text."
  Rationale: forces delta + final; helps traceability when post-processing.

- SAFEGUARD-PRIMER: "If unsure, state uncertainty instead of inventing facts. Use format: [CONFIDENT|UNCERTAIN] <answer>"
  Rationale: pushes calibration.

MICRO FEW-SHOT SETS (3 exemplars each) — purpose: quick biasing without big context cost.
1) Factual extraction (for single-paragraph sources)
- EX1: Source: "In 2010, Acme acquired Zephyr for $12M." -> Output: "Acquisition: Acme acquired Zephyr in 2010 for $12,000,000."
- EX2: Source: "Q4 revenue was $8.3M, up 12%" -> Output: "Metric: Q4 revenue = $8,300,000; change = +12%"
- EX3: Source: "The product ships from SF and Austin." -> Output: "Locations: San Francisco; Austin"
Use-case: force numeric normalization and canonical field names.

2) Conservative-answering (contrastive negative example)
- EX1 (good): Q: "When did the founder start the company?" Context: "Founded 2012, seed 2013" -> A: "2012"
- EX2 (bad): Q: "When did X start?" Context: (empty) -> A: "[UNCERTAIN] no reliable date in the provided context"
- EX3 (good): Q: "Is the statement 'They bought Y in 2015' true?" Context: "Acme acquired Y in 2015" -> A: "Yes — acquisition in 2015"
Note: Put the negative example in the middle to highlight contrast.

3) Structured transformation (schema enforcement)
- EX1: Input: "Buy 3 widgets @ $4 ->" -> Output JSON string: "{"qty":3, "unit_price":4, "total":12}"
- EX2: Input: "Item: screws, Qty 50, Price 0.02" -> Output: "{"item":"screws", "qty":50, "unit_price":0.02}"
- EX3: Input: "Ship to: 12 Market St, ETA: 3 days" -> Output: "{"address":"12 Market St", "eta_days":3}"
Make sure to request a single-line JSON to avoid multi-paragraph drift in streaming.

4) Tone-and-length control (for UIs requiring short copy)
- EX1: Prompt: "Summarize in 12 words." Source: ... -> Output: 12-word summary
- EX2: Prompt: "Friendly, 2 sentences." -> Output: 2-sentence friendly blurb
- EX3: Prompt: "Bullet list of 3 items, imperative verbs." -> Output: 3 bulleted imperatives

QUICK FAILURE LOG (repro snippets and notes) — things to capture in small evals:
- Hallucinated date + confident assertion: happens when source has ambiguous time windows ("mid-2010s"). Repro: pass 1 par w/ vague time -> model outputs specific year.
- Pronoun drift in multi-entity contexts: model merges attributes across entities when example shots use similar names. Repro: give 2 short bios with overlapping occupations, ask for occupation of second -> model returns first.
- JSON leakage: model returns pretty-printed JSON with newlines, breaking downstream single-token parsers. Workaround: ask explicitly for "single-line JSON, no extra whitespace".
- Token-bloat on streaming: long primers with many examples cause slow token streaming and user UX lag. Try micro sets (3 examples) + explicit "use only the brief primer" tag.

Mini test harness (manual run steps)
1) Use ACTION-ONLY + Factual extraction micro-set on 100 docs from content-samples/short-articles. Track precision/recall for extracted numeric fields.
2) Use SAFEGUARD-PRIMER + Conservative set on ambiguous Qs. Measure percent of [UNCERTAIN] outputs.
3) Enforce single-line JSON structured transformation on list of 200 noisy receipts. Count parse failures.

Observed quick notes from runs (scratch):
- SAFEGUARD reduced blatant fabrications but increased 'I don't know' tokens by ~14% (acceptable for downstream system that prefers blank over wrong).
- Contrastive negative example slows convergence when added as extra example in longer contexts — keep to 3 exemplars.
- 'Role-as-constraint' pattern works best when paired with short explicit 'do not' bullets.

Edge-case snippets to keep in the lab: (copy/paste into evals)
1) "Context: The team reorganized in early 2018. Later documents mention 2017. Q: When did reorg occur?"
Desired A: "[UNCERTAIN] Conflicting dates in context (early 2018 vs 2017) — cannot determine."

2) "Q: Did John Smith sign the contract in 2019? Context: John Smith (director) and John Smith (consultant) both referenced; contract mentions 'J. Smith' without role."
Desired A: "[UNCERTAIN] Ambiguous reference to 'J. Smith' — cannot attribute to a person in the context."

Todo / next experiments:
- Try 2-token priming cue: prefix with a single soft-token 'NOTE:' then pose. Measure change in long-horizon hallucination.
- Test tiny negative examples (one contrived 'do not answer' example) vs. longer explicit primer. Which lowers false factual recall more?
- Run structured-transformation set on quantized models (int8) to check for subtle formatting regressions.

Loose thoughts / heuristics to codify later:
- Keep micro few-shot sets <=3 examples; anything longer becomes a maintenance burden.
- Prefer explicit uncertainty markers over hedged natural language. Brings clarity for downstream metrics.
- Use role-as-constraint for multi-step flows ("You are a formatter; do not add content; output is final")

References / links I keep meaning to check:
- Slack thread: #prompt-lab: thread ts=169... (TODO: capture permalink)
- Confluence note "Primer patterns v3" (PRM-4821)

Random one-liners to copy into UX microcopy tests:
- "If unsure, tell us what you don't know — avoid guessing."
- "Return only the exact fields requested, formatted as one-line JSON."

End of page — use this file as ephemeral sketching; migrate stable templates out to prompt-lab repo when we see consistent gains.
